title: Workstation / Workloads & serving
description: Connect serving latency and demand with actual container usage and configured budgets.

options.content: **Serving charts need metrics from the configured SGLang endpoint.** The Kubernetes Service and an explicitly configured native loopback server can feed these charts. A running process alone does not establish scrape connectivity. Kubernetes resource and Pod panels cover Pods; use Host and GPU views for a native server's system-level resources. Select a namespace to investigate Pods. Token counters describe server work and are not a replacement for the benchmark's delivered-token timing.

panels.title: Serving metrics endpoint
panels.description: Metrics endpoint reachability only.

panels.title: Running model requests
panels.description: Total running gauge; priority breakdowns are excluded.

panels.title: Queued model requests
panels.description: Total queue gauge; priority breakdowns are excluded.

panels.title: KV token-pool usage
panels.description: Server-reported token-pool fraction. It is not the physical GPU VRAM fraction.

panels.title: SGLang queued requests
panels.description: Queue depth helps distinguish demand from idle GPUs. Priority subtotals are excluded.

panels.title: Generation token rate
panels.description: Rate of server generation-token counter per exported series. It is not per-request decode speed or verified delivered output.

panels.title: Time to first token · p50 / p95
panels.description: Observed histogram percentiles per model. Sparse traffic makes tail estimates unstable.

panels.title: Inter-token latency · p50 / p95
panels.description: Server histogram timing. Speculative stream updates may contain multiple accepted tokens; do not invert a chunk gap to estimate throughput.

panels.title: Speculative decoding · accepted tokens per step
panels.description: Mean accepted draft tokens plus the bonus token per verify step (DFlash/MTP). Only exported when speculative decoding is enabled; a falling value means the draft model is predicting the target worse.

panels.title: Speculative accept rate · prefix cache hit rate
panels.description: Share of drafted tokens accepted, and share of prompt tokens served from the prefix (radix) cache. A falling cache hit rate usually means prompts stopped sharing prefixes.

panels.title: End-to-end and queue latency · p95
panels.description: 95th percentile whole-request latency and time spent waiting in the scheduler queue. Queue time growing with end-to-end latency points at admission limits rather than kernel speed.

panels.title: Retracted and aborted requests
panels.description: Requests retracted (preempted back to the queue when the KV pool runs out) and aborted, per interval. Retractions explain latency spikes that token throughput does not.

panels.title: Prefix-cache reuse · by server
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens served from the radix (prefix) cache over the trailing hour, per server role: family is the chat service; bench, qualify and capture are AI-stack Jobs, whose prompts are deliberately fresh. 0 means prompts arrived but none reused the cache; a gap means no prompts in that hour. Series from before 2026-11-12 carry no server label.

panels.title: Family prompt tokens per hour · computed vs reused
panels.description: Prompt tokens of the family chat service over the trailing hour, split into tokens the server had to compute (prefill) and tokens reused from the prefix cache. Reuse is what keeps long multi-turn conversations responsive.

panels.title: Gateway phase
panels.description: Gateway boundary phase from its fixed-label metrics endpoint. Unavailable means the gateway is not reachable or not deployed.

panels.title: Gateway active requests
panels.description: Requests currently inside the gateway boundary.

panels.title: Gateway oldest active request
panels.description: Age of the oldest in-flight request; a growing value means a stuck or very long request.

panels.title: Gateway request results
panels.description: Requests finished by the gateway boundary per second, by fixed result class.

panels.title: Service requests (eBPF) · rate by status class
panels.description: HTTP requests per second for ai-home-lab services, measured by the host-wide eBPF collector without application changes. Empty unless TELEMETRY_EBPF is enabled.

panels.title: Service request duration (eBPF) · p95
panels.description: 95th percentile HTTP server duration per ai-home-lab service, from the eBPF collector. Streaming responses count until the stream ends.

panels.title: Container memory · actual working set
panels.description: Actual container memory working set, not its reservation.

panels.title: Container CPU · actual cores
panels.description: 1.0 means one logical CPU core of execution time.

panels.title: Memory requests and limits
panels.description: Configured budgets, not actual usage. Terminal historical Pods can still appear in kube-state-metrics.

panels.title: CPU quota throttling
panels.description: Fraction of CFS periods throttled. Missing or zero-denominator data is unavailable, not zero throttling.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{job="kubelet-cadvisor",namespace=~"${namespace:regex}",container!="",container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{job="kubelet-cadvisor",namespace=~"${namespace:regex}",container!="",container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Container restarts in the selected window
panels.description: Counter increases over the selected time window, not total lifetime restarts.

panels.title: Pod phases
panels.description: Includes retained Succeeded/Failed experiment Pods as well as currently running Pods.

panels.title: GPU compute activity by pod · AMD exporter
panels.description: Busiest card's compute activity for each pod holding GPUs. Attributed by AMD's device metrics exporter through the kubelet pod-resources API, so only pods that requested amd.com/gpu appear.

panels.title: VRAM used by pod · AMD exporter
panels.description: VRAM in use across the cards each pod holds, in MiB as reported by AMD-SMI. Attributed by AMD's device metrics exporter through the kubelet pod-resources API, so only pods that requested amd.com/gpu appear.

panels.title: AI stack build stages
panels.description: Current state of each AI-stack pipeline stage: building, or the result of its last run.

panels.title: AI stack stage duration · last run
panels.description: Wall-clock duration of each stage's most recent run.

panels.title: Compiler cache hit ratio · last run
panels.description: Share of compilations served from ccache in each stage's last run. A low ratio after a small upstream change means the cache is not being reused.

panels.title: Assistant tools · tool outcomes, not task success
Serving contract rendered for clients
panels.description: Contract identity (profile.arm) and status the gateway, Open WebUI and coding clients were rendered from (service render --serving-profile). Configuration only: it does not show that the server runs this arm. Incomplete means the render listed missing inputs; provisional means it is not yet qualified or promoted.

panels.title: Retrieval reranker state
panels.description: Configured reranker state reported by service-tools. disabled is a profile choice; missing_assets, incompatible or unknown mean retrieval runs without the configured reranker.

panels.title: Retrieval tool errors · 15 min ratio
panels.description: Share of retrieval tool calls that ended in error or unavailable over 15 minutes. no_evidence and denied are not errors. A low ratio is tool health, not answer quality.

panels.title: Retrieval tool calls by outcome
panels.description: Retrieval tool calls per second by fixed outcome. evidence means passages were returned; it does not mean the answer was correct or the user's task succeeded.

panels.title: Retrieval tool latency · p50 / p95
panels.description: Retrieval tool duration including reranking and permitted expansion, from the bounded histogram.

panels.title: Web, handoff and memory tool operations
panels.description: Operations per second by tool and fixed outcome. ok is a completed tool call; a handoff conflict is a refused stale save, shown so it can be retried, not lost work.

panels.title: Retrieval without the configured reranker
panels.description: Retrieval calls answered without the configured reranker, by reason. Results are still returned but ranked by the first-stage score.

panels.title: Embedding queue
panels.description: Requests waiting in the TEI embedding queue (Graphiti memory). Sustained values above a few mean the 4-CPU service is saturated.

panels.title: Embedding errors · 15 min ratio
panels.description: Share of embedding requests that did not succeed over 15 minutes (TEI request count minus successes). 429s from the 32-request cap count here.

panels.title: Embedding CPU throttled · 15 min
panels.description: Share of CFS periods in which the embedding container hit its 4-CPU quota (cAdvisor). High values with a growing queue mean it needs more CPU, not more threads.

panels.title: Embedding throughput
panels.description: Embedding requests by kind (single text or batch) and the texts embedded per second.

panels.title: Embedding latency · p50 / p95
panels.description: Request latency, and the queue and inference parts of it. Queue time growing while inference time is flat means demand above capacity.
